question.text: Heat of neutralization of strong acid and strong base under 1 atm and <math><msup><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><mrow><mtext>o</mtext></mrow></msup><mtext>C</mtext></math> is -13.7 Kcal/equivalent. If standard Gibb's energy change for dissociation of water to <math><msup><mrow><mtext>H</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mtext>O</mtext><msup><mrow><mtext>H</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> is -19.14 Kcal/mol, the change in standard entropy for dissociation of water in <math><mtext>cal</mtext><mtext mathvariant="normal"> </mtext><msup><mrow><mtext>K</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext mathvariant="normal">m</mtext><mtext mathvariant="normal">o</mtext><msup><mrow><mtext mathvariant="normal">l</mtext></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is:

solution.text:
Δ H o for neutralization of strong acid and base is −13.7 kcal/equivalent

H + +O H − → H 2 O

Hence, for dissociation, enthalpy change will be +13.7 kcal/equivalent

H 2 O→ H + +O H −

Δ G o for dissociation is given as: −19.14 kcal

Δ G o =Δ H o −TΔ S o

⇒   Δ S o = ( Δ H o −Δ G o ) T = 13.7−( −19.14 ) 298

⇒   Δ S o =( 32.84  kcal 298  K )=110.2  cal   K −1   mo l −1
